[](/404kidwiz/antigravityactionlaunchpad/blob/main/assets/hero.png) A lightweight, zeroframework MCP App plugin for Google Antigravity that renders native inline chat Action Launchpad cards (deck_actions) — ultracompact 1line followup pills, a zerojump hover Why / What Decision Inspector, A2UIinspired ChoicePicker chips, inline short text inputs, selectable checkboxes, and 2step ProposeThenApply approval gates. Works crossplatform (macOS, Linux, and Windows) with Node.js 20+ and ships with selfcontained prebuilt dist/ bundles (zero runtime node_modules required for end users). Surface Compatibility: Interactive inline ui:// cards render in the Antigravity App (v2.34.0+) (and any MCP client advertising io.modelcontextprotocol/ui). In Antigravity IDE (standalone), Antigravity CLI (agy), and other nonUI MCP clients, the plugin autodiscovers and runs normally — deck_actions detects the missing UI capability and automatically returns a clean numbered plaintext list with each option's Why / What rationale and parameter summary. [](/404kidwiz/antigravityactionlaunchpad/blob/main/assets/previewpills.png) [](/404kidwiz/antigravityactionlaunchpad/blob/main/assets/previewcontrols.png) Features Ultracompact 1line command rows: Edgetoedge hairlinedivided rows (1–3 \+ quiet header ghost exit + flush +N more options overflow) with zero nested card chrome. Zerojump live Decision Inspector: Hover or focus any row to crossfade its Why: and What: context in a fixedheight footer band (defaulting to the primary row — never resizes the iframe or flickers). Press d or click Details ⌄ to expand all rows inline. A2UIinspired parameter trio (optional per card): choices — Singleselect segmented controls (role="radiogroup", arrowkey navigation, clicktoclear when optional) and softened multiselect filter chips (ariapressed \+ animated checkmarks). inputs — Lightweight short text fields (e.g., branch name, tag, release note) with Enter to advance/submit, Esc to blur, and required validation. toggles — Selectable parameter checkboxes with live selected counts. ProposeThenApply approval gates (mode: "approval"): Risk badge (low / medium / high), affected targets pills, and inline 2step arming confirmation on tone: "danger" actions (Click to confirm for 4.5s, Esc cancels).

[](https://t.me/snowdensay) [](/grfdsasdvef/awesomehftcpp23internals/blob/main/LICENSE) [](/grfdsasdvef/awesomehftcpp23internals/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) 🚀 Snowden SAY Deep Systems Engineering Lab Community:Ежедневные глубокие разборы аварий на проде, memory leaks, тюнинг Linux kernel и lockfree паттерны — в нашем инженерном канале: [@snowdensay](https://t.me/snowdensay). 📚 Полная монография (все 5 глав + репозиторий с тестами): доступна в Telegramботе [@Snowden\_book\_bot](https://t.me/Snowden%5Fbook%5Fbot?start=hftexecutionsystemscpp23) 📑 Complete Curriculum Overview Module 1 (Included Below): Architectural Foundations, Memory Layouts & Invariants Module 2: HighConcurrency Core & LockFree Data Structures _(Full Handbook)_ Module 3: Production Crash Recovery, WAL & State Machine Consistency _(Full Handbook)_ Module 4: KernelBypass I/O, SIMD Acceleration & Hardware Offloading _(Full Handbook)_ Module 5: Live Incident PostMortems, Chaos Engineering & Production Benchmarks _(Full Handbook)_ Chapter 1 — Microsecond Execution Architecture: CPU Pinning, Core Isolation & OS Jitter Elimination 1.1 The Latency Budget: Where the Nanoseconds Go A wellengineered ticktotrade path on modern hardware (AMD EPYC 9004 "Genoa" or Intel Sapphire Rapids, Solarflare X2522 NIC) targets p50 ≈ 450ns, p99 < 1.8µs, p99.9 < 4µs from kernelbypass packet arrival to order wireout. The breakdown: Stage Cost Dominated by NIC DMA into userspace ring (ef\_vi/onload, DPDK) 700ns–1.1µs PCIe Gen4 x16 deserialization, PHY Parse + strategy decision 150–400ns L1/L2 residency of the hot loop Order encode + TX doorbell 300–500ns MMIO write flush, NIC TX queue Every source of _jitter_ — cache eviction, TLB shootdown, IRQ storm, SMIs, page faults — attacks the tail, not the median. Exchanges reject on tail: a 99.9thpercentile spike of 400µs on a market data handler is a loss of queue position at CME/ICE, worth measurable alpha per event. The architecture goal of this chapter: eliminate the OS as a scheduler and isolate the CPU core to behave as a deterministic coprocessor. 1.1.1 Jitter Source Taxonomy ┌──────────────────────── OS Jitter Sources (measured on bare metal, 5.15 kernel) ───────────────────────┐ │ │ │ Source Typical Spike Mechanism │ │ ─────────────────────────── ───────────── ────────────────────────────────────── │ │ SMIs (System Mgmt Interrupts) 20µs – 4ms SMM firmware runs at same privilege as │ │ hypervisor, invisible to OS. BIOS setting. │ │ Kernel preemption 2 – 50µs CFS scheduler timeslice expiry (sched_latency │ │ default 6ms) interrupts hot thread. │ │ IRQ handling (network, timers) 5 – 100µs MSIX vectors land on pinned cores w/o │ │ affinity pinning. │ │ TLB shootdown IPIs 2 – 15µs mprotect/munmap on other threads forces │ │ remote TLB invalidation via IPI. │ │ RCU callbacks / kswapd 10 – 500µs Direct/indirect reclamation, kcompactd │ │ running on your core. │ │ Timer ticks (CONFIG_HZ=250) 1 – 10µs Periodic tick + scheduler load balancing. │ │ Page faults 1 – 500µs Demand paging, minor faults, transparent │ │ hugepage collapse (khugepaged). │ │ Frequency transitions (Pstates) 20µs – 1ms Cstate exit latency (C6: up to 240µs │ │ packagewide drain on Intel). │ └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ 1.2 The Isolation Stack: Boot Kernel → IRQ Steering → Thread Affinity Isolation is a layered contract. Each layer below must hold or the layer above is meaningless. Layer 0 — Kernel boot arguments (grub) isolcpus=nohz_full,domain,managed_irq,227 remove cores 227 from scheduler domains nohz_full=227 suppress periodic tick when 1 runnable task rcu_nocbs=227 offload RCU callbacks to housekeeping cores 01 rcu_nocb_poll don't rely on IPI to kick nocb kthreads irqaffinity=01 default IRQ affinity to housekeeping cores intel_pstate=disable or amd_pstate=disable; use acpicpufreq processor.max_cstate=1 intel_idle.max_cstate=0 block deep Cstates (C6 exit = 240µs) transparent_hugepage=never khugepaged collapse = 100µs+ pauses mitigations=off optional: recovers ~7% IPC lost to retpoline/ MDS flushes; riskaccept per firm policy skew_tick=1 offset percpu timer ticks to avoid lock convoys Invariant: isolcpus with nohz_full guar

items.desc: description: Grasmere is a Markdown editor for writers and researchers, with sophisticated features to take you from an idea to a manuscript or thesis. title: Grasmere for writers & researchers image: https://grasmere.app/assets/share.jpg 01 Research Make a plan for your project. Collect your research from websites, books and papers so you can cite it later. Bring together all your tasks in one list. [Web Clipping](guides/research.htmlsavewebpage) [Highlights & Annotations](guides/research.htmlreadinghighlightsandannotations) [PDF Papers](guides/research.htmlpdfpapers) [PDF Highlights](guides/research.htmlhighlights) [BibTeX Import](guides/citations.htmlimportsources) [Zotero](guides/research.htmlfromreadwiseandzotero) [Reader Import](guides/research.htmltheresearchfolder) [Brainstorm](guides/askyourdocumentsandai.htmlbrainstorm) [Index Cards](guides/theindex.html) Research Ask Brainstorm Annotate Documents 02 Draft A pure Markdown writing experience, free from distraction. Find interesting links between your documents and brainstorm ideas with the ondevice model. [Writing](guides/writingandformatting.html) [Links](guides/linksandbacklinks.html) [Tasks](guides/tasksandduedates.html) [Journal](guides/journal.html) [Citations](guides/citations.html) [Mermaid](guides/picturesandtables.htmldiagrams) [Neat Tables](guides/picturesandtables.htmltables) [Focus Mode](guides/focusmodeandsplitview.html) [Writing Goals](guides/writinggoals.html) [Writing Replay](guides/writingreplay.html) Links & Tasks Journal Sticky Links Replay 03 Review Your reviewer uses Word. _You stay in Markdown._ [Review](guides/review.html) [Word Round Trip](guides/review.htmlsendingit) [The Margin](guides/themargin.html) [Running Order](guides/themanuscriptview.htmltherunningorder) Word Comment Reorder Step 1 Send. Export a Word file from the Review screen. Your open comments go with it. Step 2 They review. In Word, Pages or Google Docs, with comments and tracked changes as usual. They don’t need Grasmere. Step 3 Import. Drop the file back in. Every comment and change appears beside your text, ready to accept, reject or reply to. Changes you made in the meantime are kept. 04 Publish Publish your manuscript in PDF or Word Doc, complete with citations and formatting. Publish your project as a website with one click. [Manuscript](guides/themanuscriptview.html) [PDF](guides/publishing.htmlpublishafoldertopdf) [Word](guides/publishing.htmlexportadocumentasaworddocument) [Website](guides/publishing.htmlbuildawebsite) Preview Formatting Footnotes Privacy & AI Your Writing Belongs To You 01 Nothing leaves your Mac unless you send it. No account, no analytics, no tracking. Grasmere has no server. Your documents are Markdown files in folders you choose. 02 AI that runs on your Mac. Ask and Brainstorm use Apple’s on‑device model by default. They work offline and send nothing anywhere. 03 AI that leaves the writing to you. Brainstorm an essay, research or runbook. Grasmere asks you questions and you get the ball rolling. Start writing today. items.desc: description: Middle Word is a free daily word game. Find the hidden word that sits alphabetically between two others in ten guesses. A new puzzle every day. title: Middle Word: Daily Word Game — PZL games image: https://pzlgames.com/shared/assets/images/ogthemiddlev3.png Middle Word Find the word that falls alphabetically between two others. You have ten guesses, with each answer helping you narrow the search. How to play Start with two words and find the common word hidden between them in alphabetical order. After each guess, the game tells you whether the answer comes before or after your word, and how many dictionary words separate them. Use that information to narrow the gap and find the answer within ten guesses. The answer is a common word in its basic dictionary form, rather than an obscure plural or a conjugated verb. Guesses that come before the answer appear above it; guesses that come after appear below. The number shows distance in the dictionary. It is based on spelling, not meaning. There is a new puzzle each day, with earlier puzzles in the archive. Making each guess useful When the gap is wide, try a word somewhere between your closest guesses. Even if it is not the answer, it can rule out a useful part of the dictionary. Once the gap is small, think of familiar words that fit the remaining letters. The answer will be an ordinary word, so there is no need to search for something obscure. Keep your attention on spelling. “Apple” and “apply” sit close together alphabetically, even though their meanings have little in common. You can read the full guide in [How to play Middle Word](../../blog/middleword/). For a puzzle that puts meanings and sentences to work, try [Definitions](../../games/definitions/). Questions What is Middle Word? Middle Word is a free daily word game. You have ten guesses to find a common word that sits alphabetically between two given words. Each guess shows which direction to go and how far you are from the answer. How do I win Middle Word? Find the hidden word within ten guesses. Use each result to narrow the alphabetical range, then look for a common dictionary word that fits the remaining gap. Does the meaning of a word matter? No. The clues use alphabetical order only.
